items.title: Demand Forecasting & Inventory Optimization
items.summary: A LightGBM demand forecast that cut inventory cost 8.9% against a seasonal moving-average baseline while holding a 90.4% service level.

problem.text: Standard demand forecasting breaks down on **intermittent demand**, which represents 74% of the product catalogue. A model tuned only for high-volume SKUs overstocks slow movers and burns holding cost, while a model tuned for them under-forecasts the winners.

solution.title: The Solution
solution.text: A recursive LightGBM forecaster with per-SKU feature engineering, wrapped in a safety-stock policy sized from forecast variance rather than a fixed buffer.

decisions.title: Solution Overview
items: ** Multi-horizon direct forecasting with leakage free lags and rolling features, calander effects such as promotions, holidays etc.

results.text: Across a 28-day blind holdout the forecast reduced total inventory cost by **$1,601 (8.9%)** versus the seasonal moving-average baseline, while maintaining a **90.4% service level**.

items.title: Constraint Allocation
items.summary: A MILP squad builder that returns a provably optimal lineup, and reports infeasibility instead of quietly returning a bad team.

problem.text: Budget, formation balance, positional versatility, and players already decided on — each constraint is simple alone, and contradictory together. Scoring candidates by hand finds something *plausible*. It never finds the best one, and it cannot tell you when no valid squad exists.

solution.title: The Solution
solution.text: Formulated as a mixed-integer linear program so the solver returns the best available squad under the constraints, and an unsatisfiable scenario is reported as infeasible rather than silently degraded.

results.text: The returned squad is provably optimal for the given budget and formation. Scenarios that cannot be satisfied are surfaced as infeasible instead of returning a suboptimal team.
